mappings.note: Which initiatives are encouraged to help the craft survive -- pankha-making workshops. A preservation effort, C-4.3-LO-1. Not C-4.2-LO-2: no material, design or role is asked.

Workshops pass valuable skills down to YOUNGER GENERATIONS -- transmission of the craft, which is what C-4.3-LO-1's preservation covers. Not C-4.3-LO-2 (craft vocabulary carrying community knowledge): skills, not words. DEFECT: concept tag reads 'Listening and Speaking Skills', unrelated to the item.
Celebrating the craft instils PRIDE in the craftspersons -- the community's relation to its own craft, C-4.3-LO-1. Not C-4.2-LO-2, which is about the object.

Why artisans must balance ancient technique with new design -- 'to preserve traditional roots while appealing to modern consumers'. The preservation-of-roots wording is C-4.3-LO-1. Not C-4.2-LO-2, whose designs are the inherited ones.
Keeping the 'winds of change' blowing for India's ARTISTIC HERITAGE -- the craft as shared heritage, C-4.3-LO-1. Not C-2.2 despite the title phrase: the item tests the aim, not the metaphor.

A which-statements-are-correct item on state-to-material pairings, so the regional-varieties outcome C-4.2-LO-1. DEFECT, twice over: only one of the three statements survives in the stem ('Bihar utilizes the spongy sola plant centre.'), and that one statement contradicts the chapter -- sola is West Bengal's material, Bihar's is bamboo -- yet the stored key says statements 1 and 2 are correct. The item cannot be marked from the row as stored.

The chapter's underlying theme, keyed to 'the evolution, preservation, and cultural significance of the traditional hand fan'. That names two outcomes at once: preservation and cultural meaning (C-4.3-LO-1) and the evolution of the fan's roles (C-4.2-LO-2). Both cited because the correct option depends on both.
Demand now gives artisans a steady and SUSTAINABLE livelihood -- what keeps the practising community, and so the craft, alive. C-4.3-LO-1. Not C-4.2-LO-2: no role of the object is asked.

How the title works as a metaphor -- the figure itself (C-2.2 close reading of style) plus what it stands for, the fan's passage from cooling necessity to decorative artefact (C-4.2-LO-2). C-2.2-LO-12 is NOT cited even though the concept tag says "Metaphor in 'Canvas of Soil'": LO-12 is about that separate piece, not the chapter title. DEFECT: wrong concept tag.
Which climatic condition necessitated the fan's invention -- the object's origin, the history strand of C-4.2-LO-1. Not LO-2: nothing about materials, designs or later roles.

How usage varied across social classes -- a symbol of elegance in royal courts, a cooling tool in ordinary households. Two roles the fan has held, C-4.2-LO-2. Not C-4.3-LO-1, which needs preservation or identity.

Why fans were valued on the trade routes -- intricate designs made them exotic cultural goods. Designs plus cultural standing, C-4.2-LO-2. Not LO-1: no single region is at issue, the trade is pan-Indian.
How materials and designs MIRROR A REGION'S IDENTITY -- the craft-to-identity link, C-4.3-LO-1. Chosen over C-4.2-LO-2 because the question asks what the materials signify, not what they are.

Describe the craftsmanship of RAJASTHAN's fans -- zardozi in gold thread and engraved brass temple fans. A named region's varieties, C-4.2-LO-1. Not C-4.3-LO-1: royal heritage is descriptive here, no preservation argument is made.

What MATERIALS Gujarat's artisans use to decorate fans -- cotton, beads, mirror work. The question asks for the materials themselves, which is C-4.2-LO-2, where the Rajasthan item above asked for the region's style and took LO-1.

How the geographical availability of MATERIALS shapes Kerala's craft -- palm leaves into spade-shaped fans. The material-to-design link, C-4.2-LO-2. Not C-4.3-LO-1: geography, not identity, is the stated subject. DEFECT: answer ends 'Click Here to Buy book on Fl...'.

Differentiate the BASE MATERIALS of West Bengal (sola pith) and Bihar (bamboo) -- squarely the traditional-materials clause of C-4.2-LO-2. LO-1 would fit a question asking which state makes what; this one asks what the stuff is.
The DISTINCT FEATURE of Assam's fans -- woven cane, showing the local weaving skill. A region's characteristic variety, C-4.2-LO-1.

How the indigenous creators are characterised -- hardworking, using inherited skills to preserve their roots while adapting. The community that holds the craft, C-4.3-LO-1. Not C-4.2-LO-2: the artisans, not the artefact.

The threat modern technology posed to the pankha-making CRAFT -- the risk of the craft fading entirely, which is what makes preservation necessary: C-4.3-LO-1. Not C-4.2-LO-1 despite the concept tag 'Pankha: Etymology and History'; no etymology or region is asked.

How the fan's PRIMARY FUNCTION shifted -- from everyday cooling utility to decorative artefact. The role change is C-4.2-LO-2's second clause. Distinguished from the previous item, which is about the threat rather than the shift.

How the transformation INTO A DECORATIVE ARTEFACT helped artisans economically. The decorative role is the stated cause, so C-4.2-LO-2; the livelihood is the consequence, not the subject. Where an item asks about livelihood on its own I have used C-4.3-LO-1 instead.
Why consumers buy fans today -- to decorate, and to connect with India's historical and artistic HERITAGE. The heritage motive puts this at C-4.3-LO-1 rather than the decorative role alone.

Why the balance of ancient technique and innovative design is crucial -- survival of the craft while preserving traditional roots. C-4.3-LO-1. Not C-3.2: the item asks for an explanation, not for premises to be weighed.

The objective of pankha-making workshops -- passing age-old skills to younger generations so the heritage does not die out. C-4.3-LO-1's preservation, stated as an aim. DEFECT: concept tag 'Pankha: Etymology and History' does not match.

How workshops secure the craft's LONG-TERM SURVIVAL by teaching the youth. Preservation again, C-4.3-LO-1, here from the mechanism rather than the aim. DEFECT: the answer is truncated by page furniture -- 'these educational Downloaded from www.pdf.tube VITAMIN-M CHAPTER CHAPTER 4 VITAMIN-M'.

Write a dialogue in which an Electric Fan and a Pankha argue their respective value and place -- each states a position and answers the other, which is C-1.1 (agreement and disagreement with reasons, reaching a conclusion through discussion). C-2.3 added because the task is explicitly 'creative' and rests on personifying two objects, a literary device. Competency level throughout: curriculum 86 has no outcomes under CG-1, and C-2.3 has none either.

Analyse why balancing ancient technique with innovation is the key to the ECONOMIC SURVIVAL of indigenous crafts. Preservation of the craft argued at length, C-4.3-LO-1. Not C-3.2, which I have reserved for items that ask the student to reason beyond the text from its premises; here the text's own claim is being explained.

Evaluate how geography and local flora shape the diverse CULTURAL IDENTITY of Indian hand fans, with examples. The examples are the regional varieties (C-4.2-LO-1) and the conclusion is about identity (C-4.3-LO-1); the item cannot be answered without both, so both are cited.

A passage is quoted and the student must elaborate a general claim from it -- that adversity forces art to evolve. Reasoning outward from supplied premises is C-3.2, not C-3.1, which would stop at evaluating the passage. C-4.2-LO-2 added because the evidence used is the fan's shift from cooling tool to decorative artefact.

Extract on Gujarat and Kutch -- cotton fans with mirror work, bead fans with silver handles, hand-stitched leather fans, and home-based women workers. The sub-questions cover the localized community livelihood, why Gujarat is India's bead-craft centre, and vocabulary ('dainty', 'mirror'). Regional varieties (LO-1) plus their materials and decorative use (LO-2). Not C-4.3-LO-1: the livelihood sub-question asks what kind of livelihood it is, not what preserving it would mean.
